listing.name: JetStrike / SDL3 Port
listing.summary: Use your own DOS JetStrike CD-ROM data with the Windows package or a source build on Linux or Mac.

steps.title: Prepare a writable copy of your original game
steps.instruction: Use your own DOS CD-ROM installation. Keep JS_CDROM.EXE and the INTRO, DATA, GFX, MAP, MISC and PLANE directories together in a writable Game copy.

steps.title: Use the upstream Windows setup
steps.instruction: Extract the complete Windows x64 ZIP into its own folder and keep both executables and every DLL together. Open JetStrike.exe to choose your data and options. The optional Rip CD music action uses your owned CUE image and writes the 14 audio tracks under Game/MUSIC.

steps.title: Build the direct player on Linux
steps.instruction: The reviewed release has no Linux package. Use the upstream source with a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and SDL3 development files. From the repository root, run cmake -S jsport -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DJS_LAUNCHER=OFF -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD_LIBRARIES=-lm, then cmake --build build --target jsport. Keep the built jsport and its SDL3 runtime available. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used on Linux. This build has not been tested with original CD-ROM data on Linux.

steps.title: Build the direct player on Mac
steps.instruction: Use a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and the macOS SDL3 framework from SDL’s official development package. Keep SDL3.framework in a stable folder. From the repository root, run cmake -S jsport -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DJS_LAUNCHER=OFF -DSDL3_DIR="/full/path/SDL3.framework/Resources/CMake" -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH="/full/path/framework-folder", then cmake --build build --target jsport. Replace both paths with your actual framework locations. Build on the Mac you will use, so the player matches Intel or Apple Silicon. Keep the framework folder in place after building. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used. Native Mac game startup and saving have not been tested.

steps.title: Register the actual player in Portcove
steps.instruction: On Windows, choose jsport.exe as the existing installation; on Linux or Mac, choose the built jsport. Choose the player’s containing directory as the working directory. Add --game-dir and your writable Game copy as two separate arguments. Review the selected player, folder and arguments, then choose Play. The separate upstream launcher can stay open or close while its game continues.

warnings: Use your own original game files. The native port includes reconstructed original program behavior and its own separately licensed port code.

references.title: Keep your settings and progress before replacing files
references.instruction: Back up JS.CFG, js_save.000 through js_save.009 and any MUSIC folder with your working game data. Copy %APPDATA%/JetStrike/settings.ini as well. Close both the player and launcher before replacing files. Portcove keeps a launch registration. You and upstream own runtime replacement and backups. Removing the registration leaves the working files and profile in place.

references.title: SDL3 development framework for Mac
references.instruction: Get the official SDL3 development download from https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/latest. Use SDL3.framework from the macos-arm64_x86_64 folder in SDL3.xcframework. The iOS and simulator frameworks are different targets.

references.title: Other platforms
references.instruction: Windows x64 has the reviewed official package. Linux x64 uses the upstream source build described above, with no reviewed Linux package or title-run evidence. Intel Mac and Apple Silicon use the upstream source build described above. Both native architectures were built; Mac game execution remains untested, and there is no reviewed Mac package. Android has no reviewed package or mobile host integration. Those platforms do not inherit Windows or Linux observations.
